folder.title: The survey turned everyday mobility and software friction into practical responses.
folder.copy: Two multi-select summaries make the field packet more concrete. Walking was the most commonly selected travel mode, while the software responses showed a mixed picture: many residents found the tools helpful, but time, interface clarity, and feature overload remained visible barriers. Those findings informed a walking-time facility map and community materials on food safety and fraud prevention.

facts.label: SOFTWARE RESPONSES
facts.value: 43 valid entries · 46.51% said time-consuming · 44.19% said it helped clearly

facts.label: USABILITY FRICTION
facts.value: 32.56% unclear guidance/interface · 32.56% too many features · 23.26% needed help

facts.label: RESEARCH OUTPUTS
facts.value: 5 / 10 / 15-minute facility map · food-safety poster · anti-fraud lecture

folder.note: The percentages come from multi-select questionnaire summaries, so categories are not expected to total 100%. The packet connects those aggregate findings to both a digital map and community-facing materials.

notebook.meta: THERMO FISHER / ROBOTIC TUBE HANDLING / TEST PACKET
notebook.title: Three model iterations for a four-class perception-to-action workflow.
notebook.copy: A working packet of robot-camera captures, Roboflow exports, training runs, held-out comparisons, and saved real-hardware workflow frames. It traces the detector from three classes to four and the system from perception-only tests to verified pickup and placement.
notebook.note: Remaining unsuccessful runs involved intermittent camera or hardware faults. Recovery tooling restores operation, but the root cause remains unresolved.

components.meta: EMG DEVICE / CAD + HARDWARE ITERATION / REV. CURRENT
components.title: The enclosure was modeled around the real electronics.
components.copy: After building and soldering the signal path, the enclosure was developed in Fusion 360 around the ESP32 boards, battery, switch, charging access, fasteners, and internal clearances. The two CAD views document both the rounded wearable shell and the constrained component layout inside it.

envelope.meta: COURSE ALLOCATION / RESIDUAL RULE / VERSION 01 → VERSION 02
envelope.title: A random residual rule could push probability toward lower-ranked courses.
envelope.copy: When course capacity and student assignment capacity remained after the main fractional allocation, Version 1 distributed the residual pieces by randomly choosing among the remaining courses. That could add unnecessary probability mass to lower-ranked choices. Version 2 instead balanced remaining course capacity against remaining student capacity, with the project design goal of producing a more even probability matrix.

facts.label: VERSION 01
facts.value: random selection among courses with remaining capacity

facts.label: OBSERVED RISK
facts.value: unnecessary probability mass on lower-ranked courses

facts.label: VERSION 02
facts.value: balance remaining course capacity with remaining student capacity

facts.label: DESIGN GOAL
facts.value: reduce low-preference pieces · make the residual distribution more even

envelope.note: This was an algorithm-design iteration, not only a code cleanup. More even describes the project goal; the available materials do not establish a formal fairness guarantee.
